transcript.content: Tell me about your day-to-day experience with parenting—especially a recent moment when you had to set a boundary or correct your child.
We try to ignore minor bad behavior and only step in for the big stuff, positive reinforcement works better for us
What’s a recent example of “the big stuff” where you had to step in, and what did you do?
Sometimes our kid tries to override our house rules by negotiating endlessly, we just hold the line calmly
When the negotiating keeps going, what does “holding the line calmly” actually sound or look like in the moment?
We give clear instructions with just one or two steps at a time so it doesn't feel overwhelming for them
What do you most want your child to learn from the way you set boundaries?
It's tiring some days but overall I think we're doing okay
On the days it feels tiring, what is one quality you still most want your child to carry away from these boundary-setting moments?
